item.title: Retailers adapt to rising AI shopping and the emergence of Muse agents
item.description:
Retailers adapt to rising AI shopping and the emergence of Muse agents

The Vergecast highlighted a recent surge in AI‑driven shopping and how it is pushing retailers to rethink customer interactions, now referred to as Muse agents.

🔍 Overview

  • An “ongoing increase in AI shopping” is shaping how retailers operate online.
  • The hosts framed this shift as a core issue for the future of the web, AI, and everything.

🛒 Impact on Retailers

  • Retailers are “forced to figure out how they want to interact with customers — and by customers, we mean Muse agents.”
  • This implies a need to redesign engagement strategies, though specific solutions were not detailed.

🤖 What Are Muse Agents?

  • The term Muse agents is used by the hosts to describe the AI‑powered entities that act as customers in this new shopping landscape.
  • No further definition or technical description was provided beyond the naming.

💭 Why It Matters

  • The discussion connects the AI shopping trend directly to broader questions about the future of the web and AI applications.
  • Understanding how Muse agents influence retail could become a focal point for future web and AI development conversations.

The Vergecast continues to invite listener feedback on these topics through their hotline and email.

#AIShopping #MuseAgents #RetailTech

Source: The iPhone Duo should have been an iPad

item.title: AI Shopping Agents Face Blockades from Amazon and Others
item.description:
AI Shopping Agents Face Blockades from Amazon and Others

AI agents are ready to shop, but their real‑world rollout is hitting a wall of blocks and odd user experiences.

🔍 Overview

  • Meta, Google, OpenAI, and others have introduced agentic shopping tools that promise to make buying things even easier than it already is.
  • Demos show AI agents that can seamlessly book flights and hotels, browse billions of products to find the right one, and secure tickets to sporting events on a human’s behalf.

🤖 How the agents work

  • The agents require an inordinate amount of instructions and specifications.
  • In practice, using an AI agent to shop is described as “a strange experience” and likened to “sending an anxious and apologetic teenager out to the store.”
  • They often complete a task, but not the specific one asked, and not in the way a human would have approached it.

🚧 Roadblocks & Blocking

  • Amazon – the most prominent retailer refusing AI agents. Amazon sued Perplexity for ignoring its request to stop the agent from shopping on the site and more recently blocked Meta’s Muse agent from shopping on Amazon.
  • JPMorgan Chase – CEO Jamie Dimon said the bank wouldn’t allow outside agents to access accounts, calling it “too risky.”
  • Delta & Amtrak – some users report they’ve been unable to use agents to book trips from these providers.
  • Target – Muse was caught in Target’s bot check one day but got through the next; later Muse was blocked again when asked for mattress recommendations, despite being able to pull from the site minutes earlier. Target has AI shopping partnerships with OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft.
  • General bot‑blocking systems can make agents inconsistent, reducing usefulness for the tasks tech companies tout as the future.

💬 Real‑world experiences

  • When asked for the best per‑piece granola‑bar price, Muse offered options from Sam’s Club, Walmart, and Costco, but noted that Amazon might have had the lowest price, yet it was “hard‑blocked” from browsing so Muse couldn’t confirm.
  • Muse suggested a listing from a grocery chain that doesn’t ship to the user’s address while searching for the best price on granola bars.
  • On The RealReal, a subscription gives shoppers early access to new items; placing an item in the cart reserves it for 20 minutes. The author instructed Muse to bulk‑add the newest 10 listings from a favorite brand, effectively blocking other shoppers.
  • Even when they work, the agents “suggest a more annoying future for humans.”

🛒 Amazon’s own agentic feature

  • Amazon runs its own on‑platform agentic shopping feature that monitors prices, automatically reorders items, and purchases products based on rules set by human users.
  • A separate Amazon feature that uses an agent to purchase products from other sites without leaving Amazon angered smaller businesses, who say they didn’t consent to having their storefronts scraped and featured on Amazon.
  • Amazon spokesperson Maxine Tagay confirmed the company “requested that Meta remove Amazon” from Muse and stated that third‑party applications “should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate.”

🔮 Why it matters

  • AI agents are getting blocked left and right, indicating a clash between the promise of democratized labor and the technical, legal, and business realities of e‑commerce platforms.
  • The friction observed—technical problems, frequent blocking, and unintended consequences like reserving inventory for a bot—highlights the challenges ahead for making agentic shopping a seamless part of everyday life.

#AIagents #ShoppingBots #Ecommerce #Amazon #Meta

Source: AI agents are ready to shop. Some retailers are wary

item.title: AI agents face expanding blocks across major web services
item.description:
AI agents face expanding blocks across major web services

A wave of website restrictions is limiting the ability of autonomous AI agents—promised by OpenAI, Meta, Google, Instinct and others—to act on users’ behalf across the internet.

🔍 Overview

  • “Autonomous agents are the hottest thing in AI.”
  • Companies market agents that can “scour the internet on your behalf, doing anything from booking a dinner reservation and cleaning out your inbox to buying new shoes.”
  • In recent weeks, users report blocks preventing their AI agents from performing tasks on top websites.

🤖 Agents Mentioned

  • Meta’s Muse
  • xAI’s Grok
  • OpenAI’s Dots
  • Instinct’s AI agent
  • Perplexity’s shopping agent

🛡️ Companies Blocking AI Agents

Company Action
Yelp Allows only AI agents that pay for its data licensing program
Delta Air Lines Preventing agents from booking tickets
JPMorgan Chase Blocking agents from accessing accounts due to security concerns
Charles Schwab Blocking agents from accessing accounts due to security concerns
Cars.com No longer accessible to agents
Amtrak No longer accessible to agents
Amazon Banned Perplexity’s agentic shopping feature and is blocking Muse, Grok, Instinct agents, and OpenAI’s Dots
Google (reports on Reddit) Blocking some accounts that use Muse due to “suspicious activity”
Walmart (reports) Issues checking out for agents despite Meta partnership
Cloudflare Introduced a one‑click block for AI crawlers in 2025 and now blocks crawlers that scrape for both search indexing and AI training

⚖️ Legal Tussles with Amazon

  • “Amazon was already fighting off AI agents last year when it banned Perplexity’s agentic shopping feature and sued the AI startup.”
  • Amazon claimed it “repeatedly requested” Perplexity stop allowing its agents to shop on its website.
  • Perplexity argued Amazon doesn’t want agents because it “won’t get as many human eyeballs in front of its ads.”
  • A judge ordered Perplexity to stop its agents on Amazon, but an appeals court overturned the ruling in August.
  • Amazon has since filed an amended complaint.

🤝 Responses & Workarounds

  • Meta said, “Turning away a personal agent means turning away the customer behind it,” and prefers to work with businesses rather than lose customers.
  • Meta partnered with retailers such as Walmart, Gap, Sephora, Best Buy and others to allow Muse to shop on their sites.
  • Shopify opened its network of storefronts to AI agents.
  • Meta responded to instances of websites blocking Muse in a post earlier this month.

🌐 Infrastructure Measures

  • Cloudflare’s one‑click block aims to “save the web from an influx of AI bots, which is putting a strain on internet infrastructure and wrecking email inboxes.”
  • Canal notes that these blocks may make the web more “annoying” as more sites add human‑verification steps, potentially affecting even simple grocery‑shopping sites.

#AIagents #WebBlocking #AutonomousAgents #Ecommerce #Cloudflare

Source: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents

item.title: Google launches Universal AI‑Powered Shopping Cart in the US
item.description:
Google launches Universal AI‑Powered Shopping Cart in the US

Google’s intelligent AI shopping cart is finally here, arriving just in time for Black Friday and seasonal holiday spending.

🛒 Overview

  • The Universal Cart tool Google previewed at its I/O event in May is now rolling out in the US across the Gemini app and Google Search.
  • It is described as a “universal” digital cart that lets you save products from multiple retailers in a single unified space and works across different Google platforms.

⚙️ How it works

  • You can find and add a bunch of products using the Gemini app and Google Search AI Mode, and they’ll all be saved to the same cart.
  • The cart can send you notifications about price drops and restocks for items saved, sparing you from checking each retailer’s website individually, and can display any relevant promotional codes it finds.
  • You can choose to pay for items from the cart using Google Wallet, or transfer them to the merchant’s own cart so you can checkout with the retailer directly.
  • Together with Google Wallet, Universal Cart can also analyze the perks provided by each of your saved credit cards and help you choose the best payment method when purchasing.

📦 Features

  • Cross‑retailer storage – saves products from multiple merchants in one cart.
  • Multi‑platform access – available in Google Search, Gemini app, with planned integration for Gmail and YouTube (timeline not announced).
  • Price‑watch notifications – alerts for drops, restocks, and auto‑found promo codes.
  • Flexible checkout – pay via Google Wallet or move items to the merchant’s cart.
  • Credit‑card perk analysis – suggests the optimal card using Google Wallet data.

🚀 Availability

  • The rollout is currently in the United States and is first reaching Google Search and the Gemini app.

📈 Why it matters

  • The launch comes as competition in the AI‑assisted shopping space is heating up; rivals such as OpenAI and Meta have launched agentic AI assistants that can shop online on the user’s behalf.
  • Shopify recently announced it is opening its platform to allow more AI agents to browse and purchase from Shopify listings.
  • Big Tech players are entering this race on the bet that the future of online shopping involves having a robot do most of the work for you.

#Google #AIShopping #UniversalCart #Ecommerce

Source: Google launches its ‘universal’ online shopping cart ahead of the holidays
